features.text: Creating a scene from an uploaded image opens calibration with the three methods; after calibration a 5-ft reference feature measures 5 ft ± 0.1 ft with the ruler.
Activating a scene moves every player within 2 s with a transition, and players receive only the new scene's entities.
A DM can edit a non-active scene while players remain on the active one; players receive no data from the prep scene (asserted by network inspection in a test).
features.evidence: packages/server/src/test/board.test.ts › AC-SCN-03: the DM edits a non-active scene through prep.open while a player stays on the active one; the player's raw WebSocket frames (ws-recorder) contain none of the prep scene's ids, names or entities, and its state never changes; the DM receives prep.patch updates

features.text: A GLB map can be positioned, rotated and scaled; **Generate walls** produces editable, merged, simplified wall segments from the mesh slice.
Procedural floors (stone, wood, grass, sand, parchment, cavern) render with no image asset and tile without visible seams.
Newly admitted players' characters without a token on the active scene are auto-placed around the party spawn point without overlapping walls or other tokens.
Changing a scene's ambient light or fog mode applies live for all clients within 500 ms.
Recalibrating an image map rescales walls, zones, lights and tokens so that they stay aligned with the map art.
The board renders the table environment and map at 1 unit = 1 ft, and loads nothing from outside the server (zero CSP violations and zero non-origin requests in the E2E network log).
Camera controls work as specified (zoom toward cursor, orbit, pan, presets Shift+1/2/3 and T with 400 ms transitions, pitch and distance clamps, bounds clamp).
Performance tiers are auto-selected, adapt at runtime, and can be pinned by the user; Low disables shadow maps, bloom and ambient occlusion and caps DPR at 1.
DM Spotlight moves all opted-in players' cameras to the target over 600 ms.
The first-load intro and scene transitions show no white flash and no layout jump.
Image maps up to 16 384 × 16 384 source pixels are accepted and displayed using a variant that fits the device's texture limit.
Tokens support 3D model, standee, coin and auto modes; switching is immediate and persisted.
Base diameters follow size (2.5 / 5 / 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 ft) or a custom value; the base ring shows the owner colour or the disposition colour.
Uploaded GLB minis are automatically grounded, centred, oriented and scaled to their size category, with per-asset overrides that persist.
The overlay shows the name, the HP bar, and up to 6 condition icons directly under the bar with "+N" overflow; HP display modes Exact/Bar/Descriptor/Hidden work per token.
Damage animates a trailing ghost segment (400 ms hold, 600 ms drain); temp HP is a separate segment; a tick marks 50% HP.
Right-click or long-press opens a radial menu containing only actions the viewer is permitted to perform.
Flying tokens can be raised or lowered in 5-ft steps (Alt+wheel or a HUD stepper) and show a stem, ground ring and elevation label; measured distances include the vertical component.
DM-hidden tokens render at 40% opacity with an eye-slash badge for DMs and are never present in any player's state.
The Quick Unit dialog creates a sheetless unit with arbitrary values in one submit.
Twenty tokens using the same GLB share geometry and materials (renderer memory info shows one geometry set, not twenty).
Auto mode crossfades between coin and standee at a camera pitch of 70°.
The hover card appears after 400 ms and shows AC only to the DM and the token's owners.

Linked and unlinked tokens behave as specified: goblins spawned from one Bestiary entry keep separate HP and conditions; a player character shows the same HP and conditions on every scene; unlinking a token copies the current values; relinking asks before overwriting.

In combat on their own turn, dragging a token shows a routed path around walls with a distance/remaining label; the in-budget part is verdigris, the rest ember-red, with a max-reach marker at the exact budget point.
The client preview cost equals the server's authoritative cost within 0.05 ft for 200 randomised shared-test scenarios.
Difficult terrain doubles the cost of the part of the path inside it, and the label shows the difficult portion.
Releasing beyond budget clamps the move to the max-reach point by default; with *Overlong moves: reject* the move is refused with an explanation.
**Reset move** returns the token to its turn-start position and restores the full budget; allowed any time during the owner's turn under the default rule.
Ctrl/Cmd+Z after a move undoes only the last segment and refunds its cost.
Players cannot move tokens they don't control; in combat they can move only on their own turn unless granted free movement; DM moves ignore budgets unless "Count as movement" is ticked.
The server rejects path segments that cross movement-blocking walls; walls hidden from the player truncate the move at the contact point with the "unseen" toast.
Dash adds the current speed to the budget; Stand up costs half speed; crawling while prone doubles cost; speed-zero conditions block movement with a message.

The movement range overlay shows the reachable region around walls and difficult terrain (remaining budget in combat, speed in exploration), with the limit isoline within 1 ft of the true geodesic limit in test scenes.
Ruler, radius, cone (53.13°), line and cube tools show live distances in the campaign's units and are shared to others for 3 s by default.
Feet display rounds to 0.5 ft; metres use 5 ft = 1.5 m and round to 0.1 m; all internal maths is in feet.
Viewers who can see a token see its drag preview (≤ 15 Hz) and the committed move animating along the path at 30 ft/s (250 ms–2 s).
Holding Alt while dragging switches to freehand; collisions truncate the freehand path.
A path that leaves a visible hostile creature's reach shows an opportunity-attack marker at the exit point, suppressed while the mover is Disengaged.

Creature-space rules are enforced for players when *Enforce creature spaces* is on (ending overlap blocked; allies passable; passable non-ally spaces cost double; other non-allies block), and ignored for DM moves.
Ctrl/Cmd+click waypoints route the path through each waypoint in order, the total cost includes all legs, and a plain click or Enter commits.
DM bonus movement (+X ft for this turn / N rounds / until removed) adds to the budget per §19.4 (not doubled by Dash), shows in the budget label ("30 + 10 ft"), and expires as set.
The six wall kinds (door with closed/open/locked states) follow the blocking matrix exactly, verified by unit tests on the shared blocking predicates.
Wall drawing supports chaining, 1-ft endpoint snapping, Shift angle snapping to 15°, Ctrl/Cmd to disable snapping, the Room tool, and Backspace to remove the last placed segment while drawing.
Players can open/close unlocked doors within 5 ft; locked doors refuse with a lock indicator; DMs can toggle any door; paths and vision update within 200 ms.
Secret doors are indistinguishable from walls in players' state until revealed (no door flag, no door handle, same kind value as a wall).
Zones of each kind behave as specified; hazard triggers create DM prompts at the right moments.
"Walls in 3D" extrudes walls with a stone material and animates doors opening and closing.
Editing stays responsive (under 16 ms per frame) with 1 000 wall segments in a scene.

Painted mode: brush/rectangle/polygon reveal and hide work (for all players or chosen players); Reveal room fills the wall-enclosed region under the cursor; players see only their revealed areas and the tokens inside them. (Undo of fog operations is covered by AC-UNDO-01.)
Dynamic mode: each player sees only what their own character(s) can currently perceive; previously seen areas remain as desaturated memory without creatures.
A token carrying a torch lights 20 ft bright plus 20 ft dim, blocked by walls, with flicker; owners can toggle their token's light.
In darkness, a character with 60 ft darkvision sees within 60 ft rendered in greyscale; dim light within range renders as bright; unlit areas beyond range are not visible.

Two players in the same dark room: A (darkvision) sees goblin G, B (no darkvision, no light) does not; B's client state never contains G (asserted via the test hook and by inspecting WebSocket frames).
Magical darkness blocks darkvision and nonmagical light; truesight and blindsight within range see through it.
Heavily obscuring effects block sight into and through their area; a viewer inside one sees only their own space; lightly obscuring effects render a haze without blocking.
Invisible creatures are visible only to viewers with truesight or blindsight in range, See Invisibility, or while outlined by Faerie Fire.
Tremorsense shows a sensed marker (no name, appearance or HP) for grounded creatures in range that are not otherwise seen.
DMs see all with a hatched fog overlay; **View as** reproduces a player's rendering exactly and changes nothing for other clients.
A viewer who loses sight of a creature mid-move sees it travel only to the last visible point on the path and never receives its destination.
Server vision recomputation for 8 viewers, 500 walls and 50 lights takes under 10 ms at p95 on the host; client fog reveals animate over 300 ms.
Vision sharing is off by default; the DM can share a token's vision with chosen players or enable party vision.
Explored memory persists across server restarts per player and scene; the DM can reset it per player or for everyone.
Blinded creatures provide no sight-based vision (blindsight and tremorsense still apply); Unconscious creatures provide no perception at all.
The formula grammar in §18.1 is fully supported and invalid formulas show inline errors without submitting.
All outcomes are generated on the server with `crypto.randomInt`; the client never decides a result.
3D dice for d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20 and d100 (two d10s) always come to rest showing exactly the server's values.
Public results reach everyone within 300 ms of the server result; Private-to-DM shows to the roller and DMs; Blind shows only to DMs (the roller sees "?"); Self shows only to the roller.
Manual entries are recorded with a hand icon and are visible to everyone like normal rolls.
Roll requests deliver a card with Roll / Enter / Skip to each target, show the DM live status and success/failure against a hidden DC, and allow the DM to roll for a player.
Each player's dice skin is visible to everyone for that player's rolls.
Dice sounds are triggered by simulated contacts, with volume scaled by impulse.
Limits are enforced: at most 100 dice per term and 500 dice rolled in total (including rerolls and explosions), at most 1 000 sides, explosion depth at most 20, formula length at most 200 characters.
In test mode only, `GLOAM_TEST_SEED` makes results reproducible; production builds ignore it.
Condition-derived advantage/disadvantage hints are applied to relevant rolls and can be removed by the roller before rolling.
Quick create makes a playable character (name, class/level, HP, AC, speed, darkvision, art) in one dialog.
Derived values compute correctly (unit tests against worked examples) and every derived field can be overridden and reverted.
Custom blocks of all seven types can be added, renamed, reordered and deleted; counters can be pinned to the token as an extra bar.
Sheet templates can be saved and used to create new characters.
The three lock levels restrict exactly the specified fields; proposals on locked fields reach the DM with a diff and apply only on approval.
JSON import validates against the published schema, shows a preview/diff, and rejects invalid input with readable errors; export → import round-trips losslessly.
The Import-with-AI dialog copies a prompt that contains the current JSON Schema and the conversion rules from Appendix F.3.
Every roll-able element rolls the right formula; Alt/Ctrl modifiers and the touch long-press menu set advantage/disadvantage.
Sheet changes to HP, temp HP, conditions, speeds, senses, size and light update the linked token within 200 ms.
The drawing pad produces a transparent PNG with pressure-sensitive strokes and undo/redo, usable as portrait and token art.
Paper cutout turns a photo of a drawing on white paper into a clean transparent sticker, with adjustable tolerance and outline.

The damage pipeline implements the SRD 5.2.1 order exactly (modifiers and save halving → resistance → vulnerability; immunity zero), then temp HP absorbs first; at least 30 table-driven unit tests pass.
Healing never exceeds max HP; healing a creature at 0 HP restores consciousness and resets death saves.
Gaining temp HP while having some offers keep or replace, defaulting to the higher value.
All 15 SRD conditions and all listed status markers can be added and removed from the token menu, the sheet and the DM panel, each with a unique icon, name and summary tooltip.
Exhaustion shows its level; −2 × level applies to d20 tests and −5 ft × level to speed; level 6 prompts the DM.
Bloodied is applied and removed automatically at the half-HP threshold when enabled.
Damage to a concentrating creature prompts a CON save with DC max(10, ⌊dmg/2⌋) capped at 30; failure ends concentration and linked effects, undoably.
A PC at 0 HP goes Unconscious and gets death save prompts at the start of each of its turns; natural 20, natural 1, 3 successes and 3 failures behave as specified.
Damage at 0 HP adds a failure (two on a critical hit); massive damage prompts the DM for instant death.
An NPC reaching 0 HP prompts the DM with Dead / Unconscious / Keep at 0, defaulting to Dead.
Floating typed damage numbers, hit shake/flash, heal glow and death animation play for everyone who can see the token.
Every automatic consequence (damage, condition, concentration loss, death) can be edited or skipped by the DM before it applies.

Short and long rests apply the rules pack's recovery (Hit Dice spending with roll/enter/skip cards; HP, Hit Dice, slots, feature uses, exhaustion and temp HP per §34.2) to the chosen characters as one undoable command with a per-character preview.
The start dialog supports all four initiative methods, participant selection, grouping identical NPCs, and per-participant surprise.
Player initiative cards offer Roll / Enter / Skip with automatic advantage/disadvantage from Invisible, Incapacitated and Surprised.
Identical NPCs can share one initiative roll.
The tracker shows portraits in order, the round number and the active highlight; players don't see combatants they can't perceive.
Turn start resets the budget and pips, runs start-of-turn prompts, plays the chime for the owner, and focuses the camera if opted in.
During combat only the active combatant's controller can move it (unless free movement is granted); End turn advances; Next/Previous/Delay/Add/Remove/Set initiative/drag-reorder work for the DM.
Stop combat returns to exploration and logs a combat summary.
Action pips track usage, are marked automatically by app-driven attacks and spells, can be toggled manually, and the Reaction resets at the start of the creature's own turn.
Effect durations tick in rounds relative to their creator's turn and expire with a notification.
Ties are broken by Dex modifier, then PCs before NPCs, then name, unless a house rule says otherwise.
Quick start begins combat in one click with all non-hidden creatures on the scene and the default initiative method, and Stop combat returns everyone to free movement in one click.
The SRD 5.2.1 pack loads exactly 339 spells with per-level counts 27, 57, 57, 42, 34, 38, 31, 20, 17, 16 (cantrip → 9th), asserted at startup and in tests.
features.evidence: packages/server/src/content/packs.test.ts › loads exactly 339 spells…; startup assertion in packages/server/src/content/packs.ts; packages/content/scripts/verify.test.ts

features.text: The spell browser searches and filters by level, school, class, casting time, concentration, ritual, damage type, save and area shape.
Casting chooses a slot (with upcast scaling), shows area templates with range rings and line-of-effect validation, supports multi-target selection, and applies self spells immediately.
Area targeting detects affected creatures per §17.3, and the DM can add or remove targets on the card.

The resolution card handles attack rolls, save requests, NPC one-click saves, damage/healing rolls, half/none on save, resistances/vulnerabilities/immunities, conditions, editable finals, and Apply/Apply all/Skip/Cancel & refund.
Slots are consumed on cast and restored on cancel or undo; rituals and free casts can skip slot use.
Casting a second concentration spell prompts to end the first; ending concentration removes linked effects.
The 16 named persistent effects behave as specified (duration, attachment, movement, light/obscurement/darkness integration with vision, difficult terrain, trigger prompts).
Each of the 12 VFX presets plays on cast, and persistent areas animate subtly within the performance budget.
The homebrew builder validates every field with a live preview; players' proposals require DM approval; SRD spells can be duplicated as templates.
JSON import via the UI and REST validates against the published schema, supports dry runs, and resolves conflicts by skip/overwrite/rename. (The MCP path is covered by AC-API-04.)
Weapon attacks and features use the same resolution card flow.
The cover hint appears on attack and save cards and matches the §17.5 algorithm in unit tests.
Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y) undo and redo the user's own token moves, token edits, fog operations, wall edits, damage/healing applications, condition changes and sheet edits.
A conflicting undo is refused for players with an explanation; DMs can force it.
The History panel lists and filters entries; Revert and Restore-to-here work with a confirmation summary.
An accidental fog wipe, a deleted token and a doubly applied damage can each be restored in at most two clicks.
Dice rolls, joins, kicks, bans, approvals, emotes, pings and music playback are not undoable.
Every accepted command is persisted in the same SQLite transaction as its history entry before any broadcast (verified by an integration test that inspects the database inside the broadcast hook).

features.text: After SIGKILL mid-session and a restart, the board, tokens, combat state, sheets, effects and fog reveals are intact; at most the last 5 s of explored memory may be missing.
Automatic snapshots run every 10 minutes (last 24 kept), on scene activation, on close and on shutdown; manual named snapshots work; restoring creates a pre-restore snapshot first.
features.evidence: packages/server/src/test/persistence.test.ts › AC-PER-03 (auto every interval with 24 kept, close, shutdown, manual named, pre-restore on restore) + packages/server/src/test/board.test.ts › AC-PER-03 (activation clause: each scene.activate writes a 'scene' snapshot)

Clients show a reconnecting banner on disconnect and resynchronise without a reload after the server returns.

Only the listed formats are accepted, detected by content; everything else is rejected with a readable reason.

features.text: All built-in sound events in §31 play from runtime synthesis with no audio files, routed through the six channels with volume and mute.

The DM music player supports upload, playlists, play/pause/next/previous/loop/shuffle/stop and a 2-s crossfade; every client stays within 75 ms of the server timeline (so within 150 ms of each other); late joiners start at the current position.
The six ambience layers are synthesized procedurally, mixed by the DM, and heard by everyone.
Audio unlocks on the first user gesture, with the enable-sound chip as a fallback.
Board sounds are stereo-panned by screen position and attenuated by distance.

The four generative music presets play continuously without audible loop points for at least 10 minutes, crossfade with each other and with uploaded tracks, and stay in sync across clients like tracks do.
The emote wheel offers 12 emotes, 8 quick phrases and up to 6 custom phrases; emotes display for 2.5 s above the token or portrait with animation and sound; the rate limit applies.
Pings appear for everyone in the sender's colour; the DM Spotlight ping also moves opted-in cameras.
Hand raise shows on the portrait and the tracker and notifies the DM once.
Handouts and secret notes reach exactly the chosen recipients with the reveal animation and stay in their Handouts list.
The campaign log records the automatic events, accepts manual entries, groups by session, and exports Markdown.
Every DM section listed is reachable within two clicks or taps, and `Ctrl/Cmd+K` jumps to any section or command by name.
All per-token overrides work and are shown as badges in the DM's token hover card.
Act as lets the DM control any character; resulting log entries and history entries record "DM as <character>".
The Approvals inbox aggregates knocks, uploads, sheet proposals and homebrew proposals with a live badge count.
DM notes (per scene and per token) are never sent to players (asserted in a test).
All sections listed exist and work end to end.
People management supports rename, PIN set/clear, DM assignment, kick, ban/unban and delete with character reassignment.

The Admin has every DM capability in every campaign plus the admin-only actions; admin sessions expire after 12 hours of inactivity; by default the Admin can log in only from the host PC (setting: allow admin login through the doorway).
The Security log records logins, failed logins, knocks, approvals, denials, kicks, bans, invite rotations, API token use and rejected uploads, with time and client IP.
About & Credits shows the exact SRD 5.2.1 attribution statement (Appendix I) and the licences of bundled fonts and libraries.
The first-run checklist tracks the five steps and disappears when all are done.
Layouts work at 360×740, 390×844, 844×390, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1440×900 and 1920×1080 with no horizontal scrolling and no overlapping controls (screenshot review).
All listed gestures work (Playwright touch emulation tests for drag-to-move, pinch zoom and long-press menu).
Touch targets are at least 44 × 44 px; HUD text is at least 12 px.

In Playwright WebKit (iPhone) and Chromium (Pixel) emulation: audio unlocks on the first gesture, the layout uses `100dvh`, the board doesn't rubber-band scroll, and drags keep pointer capture; `docs/HOSTING.md` includes a short manual checklist for real phones.

On the Low tier at DPR 1 the benchmark scene (§37) holds at least 30 fps in **headed** Chromium on the host GPU with 4× CPU throttling (a proxy for a mid-range phone; headless WebGL is software-rendered and not representative).
All DOM UI is keyboard-operable with a visible focus ring, and icon-only buttons have accessible names (axe-core check on the main screens has no serious violations).
Reduced motion disables camera flights, shake, dice tumbling and parallax.
The colour-blind palette swaps the specified colours and adds the patterns.
UI scale works from 90% to 130% without layout breakage; body text contrast is at least 4.5:1.
Every sound event has a visual counterpart.
REST v1 endpoints accept session cookies or bearer tokens and enforce scopes; tokens are shown once and stored hashed.
API tokens are refused on requests carrying Cloudflare headers unless Allow remote API is enabled.
JSON Schemas are served for every import format and match the zod schemas (a test regenerates and diffs them).
The MCP server passes a round-trip test with an MCP client: list tools, import 3 spells (dry run, then real), import 1 character, read the log.
The Connect Claude page shows working setup instructions with the real repository path and a freshly created token.
Creating the demo campaign produces the Lantern Crypt with all listed elements, using no external or uploaded assets.
The demo showcases lighting (sconces flicker, darkness pocket blocks darkvision), fog of war (dynamic), a secret door, water and difficult terrain, and a ready-to-run combat.

A scripted E2E test of the first-run flow (setup → demo → open table locally → join as a test player in a second browser context → admit → move a token) completes in under 3 minutes of wall-clock time, and every step shows guidance text a first-time user can follow.
Every REST body and room message is validated with a strict zod schema (unknown keys rejected, numbers range-checked, strings length-capped); invalid input never reaches domain code (fuzz test).

features.evidence: packages/server/src/test/security.test.ts › AC-SEC-06 secrets never appear in logs, API responses or client state

features.text: Hidden information (hidden tokens, secret doors, hidden walls other than as anonymous occluders, carried lights' and effects' token links while the carrier isn't perceived, DM notes, NPC exact HP and AC when not permitted, blind roll results, other players' private rolls, other scenes' prep data) never appears in a player's received WebSocket frames (automated frame inspection in the E2E suite).
The data directory and `secret.key` are created with owner-only permissions where the OS supports it.

features.text: `pnpm audit --prod` shows no known high or critical vulnerabilities at the end of the build, or each exception is justified in DECISIONS.md.

The benchmark scene holds 60 fps median (p95 frame ≤ 20 ms) on the High tier at 1080p in headed Chromium on the host machine; the bench report records that machine's CPU/GPU. (Target hardware class: Apple M1 / Intel Iris Xe.)
The initial table-route JavaScript is at most 1.2 MB gzipped (the dice physics worker loads lazily and is prefetched when idle).
Server command handling is under 5 ms at p95 and vision recomputation under 10 ms at p95 in the benchmark.
A player joining an already-loaded scene sees the board within 4 s on a 20 Mbps connection (assets cached afterwards).
No frame drops longer than 100 ms from shader compilation during play (shaders precompiled with `gl.compileAsync`/warm-up during the intro).
All UI colours, type sizes, spacing, radii and motion come from the tokens in §27 (no stray hex values outside the token file, enforced by a lint script).
None of the banned patterns in §27.6 appear in the final screenshots (visual-critic check).
Every custom icon in Appendix G is implemented as a React component and in the WebGL icon atlas, and renders crisply at 16, 20 and 24 px.
The first-load sequence (candle ignition → board fade-in → staggered HUD) runs once per load and respects reduced motion.
Empty states, loading states and error states exist for every panel (no blank panels).
Fonts are self-hosted from `@fontsource` packages; no font request leaves the origin.
